rv.q: The masterstroke this time out is to bring to the material much the same tongue-in-cheek spirit one might invest in a Palladium Christmas panto.
The show is still a winner that lives up to the daft excess of its title.

Jason Donovan is full-on camp-tastic as Pharaoh in golden loincloth and sparkly trainers. The choreography (JoAnn M Hunter) feels wooden at times...but there is no denying that, as a whole, this Joseph has mojo.
Occasionally John Cameron’s orchestrations drown the lyrics and one or two ideas, such as guitar-wielding statues, prove there is no lack of corn in Egypt. But this is an ebullient production...
That jaunty sense of fun permeates director Laurence Connor's constantly inventive new vision for the show, which is mostly a steamroller of pure joy and comic delights.
It's a production far surpassing any of the various London and Broadway Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoats I have come across over the last 30 years or more.
Enjoyable as it is, it's all a bit relentless.

cn.t: Critics praise this exuberant Palladium production as highly entertaining, with standout performances from newcomer Jac Yarrow in the title role and Sheridan Smith as Narrator bringing fresh energy to Lloyd Webber and Rice's beloved musical.
